title: Unauthenticated basket cookie is deserialized with pickle
description: The basket cookie is attacker-controlled but is passed directly to pickle.loads. A remote attacker can submit a crafted cookie that executes arbitrary Python code in the web application's process whenever a basket endpoint reads it.
evidence: read_basket() obtains request.cookies['basket'], base64-decodes it, and calls pickle.loads(raw) without a signature or integrity check; the cookie is created only with base64(pickle.dumps(...)) in with_basket().

title: Token refresh accepts unsigned attacker-created JWTs
description: The refresh endpoint explicitly disables JWT signature verification and only checks that the token's subject belongs to a user. An attacker can forge a token naming any user, including a staff user, and exchange it for a valid signed access token.
evidence: refresh() calls jwt.decode(token, options={'verify_signature': False}), loads claims.get('sub'), and then returns make_token(user) without validating the original token's signature, issuer, or token type.

title: JWT signing key is hard-coded in source
description: The production configuration contains a fixed, source-visible SECRET_KEY. Anyone who obtains the repository can mint valid JWTs for arbitrary user IDs and roles accepted by the application, enabling account and staff impersonation.
evidence: SECRET_KEY is assigned the literal value 'hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d' and is used by auth.make_token() and auth.user_from_request() for HS256 JWT signing and verification.

title: Authenticated users can view any order by ID
description: The order detail endpoint authenticates the caller but does not verify that the requested order belongs to that caller. Order status, totals, payment amounts, delivery information, item data, and refunds are exposed by guessing or enumerating order IDs.
evidence: show_order() returns order_json(get_order(order_id)); get_order() selects only by id, while the ownership check exists separately in own_order() and is not used by this endpoint.

title: Product search concatenates the query into SQL
description: The public search endpoint interpolates the q parameter directly into a SQL statement. An unauthenticated attacker can alter the WHERE clause and use UNION-style SQL injection to extract records from other tables, including user and payment-related data.
evidence: The query is built as "SELECT * FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%" + q + "%' OR sku LIKE '%" + q + "%' ORDER BY name LIMIT 50" instead of using a bound parameter.

title: Admin review report is injectable through a display name
description: A display name, which can be set by a normal user, is inserted into the review report SQL using an f-string. A user can choose a SQL fragment as their display name and have it executed when a staff member requests the report for that user.
evidence: reviews_by_customer() executes f"WHERE r.author_name = '{customer['display_name']}' ORDER BY r.id DESC" with no SQL escaping or parameter binding.

title: Review bodies are stored and rendered as trusted HTML
description: Authenticated users can submit arbitrary review text, and the product template renders it with the safe filter. A malicious review can therefore execute JavaScript for every visitor to the public product page, including staff users.
evidence: add_review() inserts the unescaped body directly into reviews.body, while product.html renders r.body with {{ r.body|safe }}.

title: Payment status timeouts are treated as successful payments
description: If the payment provider times out, the checkout endpoint assumes the payment is paid and moves the order to processing. A provider outage or targeted request disruption can therefore cause fulfillment of unpaid orders.
evidence: The except requests.Timeout branch sets status = 'paid', after which the normal status == 'paid' branch sets status to processing and paid_pence to total_pence.

title: Signed payment webhook does not validate the paid amount
description: Any accepted paid webhook marks an order as processing using the caller-supplied amount, without requiring it to equal the order total or be positive. A forged or faulty provider event can mark an underpaid or zero-paid order as paid and fulfilled.
evidence: For status == 'paid', the handler executes UPDATE orders SET status = 'processing', paid_pence = int(event.get('amount_pence', 0)) without comparing amount_pence with order.total_pence.

title: Image importer follows redirects outside the host allowlist
description: The URL is checked before the request, but requests.get follows HTTP redirects by default and the final destination is never validated. A resource on an allowlisted host that redirects to an internal address can make the server fetch internal services.
evidence: check_url(url) validates only the initial parsed hostname, then requests.get(url, timeout=10, stream=True) is called without allow_redirects=False or validation of r.url/history.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted fast SHA-256 hashes
description: User passwords are hashed with a single unsalted SHA-256 operation. If the SQLite database or a backup is obtained, the hashes can be cracked quickly with commodity hardware and reused against users elsewhere.
evidence: hash_password() returns hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() with no salt or work factor; this value is stored as users.password_hash.
